title: Interacting hydrodynamic modes in spinless fermions with dephasing noise
authors: Fabian H. L. Essler, Patrik Penc
abstract: We study the non-equilibrium dynamics of spinless fermions with dephasing noise in the framework of a many-particle Lindblad equation. Using a mapping to the exactly solvable one-dimensional Hubbard model with purely imaginary tunneling amplitude we analyze the Heisenberg-picture dynamics of operators quartic in fermions and determine their hydrodynamic projections. We construct the relevant diffusive eigenoperators explicitly and show that, in the quartic sector, they can be interpreted as interacting pairs of bilinear hydrodynamic modes. As a consequence, translationally invariant quartic operators generically exhibit non-vanishing diffusive late-time tails, unlike translationally invariant bilinears. Our results show that the hydrodynamic tails of microscopic operators cannot in general be inferred from symmetry constraints or coarse-grained fluctuating hydrodynamics alone; they also depend crucially on the spatial structure and effective size of the hydrodynamic eigenoperators.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how spinless fermions behave far from equilibrium when subjected to dephasing noise. By analyzing the dynamics using Lindblad equations and spectral methods, the authors prove that higher-order correlation functions exhibit persistent diffusive tails at late times. This demonstrates that simple symmetry arguments are insufficient to predict transport properties in dissipative quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The study determines the non-equilibrium dynamics and asymptotic late-time tails of correlation functions for spinless fermions subjected to dephasing noise.
main_result: Quartic operators generically exhibit diffusive power-law decay tails, unlike bilinear operators which vanish exponentially, showing that hydrodynamic behavior depends on operator structure rather than just symmetry.
method: The analysis uses the many-particle Lindblad equation, mapping it to an imaginary-time Schrödinger equation and analyzing the spectral properties of the dual Lindbladian eigenoperators.
model_or_system: The system is spinless fermions hopping on a ring lattice governed by a tight-binding Hamiltonian, whose evolution is described by a many-particle Lindblad equation incorporating dephasing noise ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Time evolution of Heisenberg-picture operators, specifically quadratic and quartic correlation functions $\langle c^\dagger_{x}c_{y} angle$ and higher order terms.
important_parameters: Dephasing rate ($\gamma$), hopping amplitude ($J$), and the asymptotic time limit ($t \gg \gamma^{-1}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on decoupling approximations (like BBGKY hierarchy) and assumes that late-time behavior is governed by eigenstates with real part of energy near zero.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail deriving asymptotic expressions for correlation functions $\Psi^{(0)}_{\{d,d,0\}}(x, t)$ showing power-law decay.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the governing Lindblad dynamics, analyzing quadratic operators first to show their behavior, and then extending this rigorous analysis to quartic (and higher) operators to prove the existence of non-vanishing hydrodynamic tails.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete example of how dissipation fundamentally alters long-time transport properties in interacting quantum systems, offering insights applicable to open quantum systems studied in AMO physics.
